subject: Default capture scope: what we keep for requests vs generated outputs
messages:
From: Sarah Cole <sarah.cole@brightbank.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.ai>
Cc: BrightBank Security <security@brightbank.com>
Date: 2028-03-20T09:12:00-04:00
Subject: Quick clarification on what Redwood keeps by default (requests vs outputs)

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks for taking this. We're finalizing our vendor risk questionnaire and a few reviewers asked for explicit language on your default capture behavior. Could you confirm the default retention window and what types of items Redwood keeps by default for hosted API customers? In particular: 

- Do you retain raw customer requests (prompt text) by default, or only metadata?
- Are model-generated outputs stored by default? If so, how long?
- How do you treat streaming fragments or KV cache artifacts versus finalized completions?

We need plain-language bullets to paste into our internal memo. Also, if you have a short example (e.g., a 3-bullet capture matrix) that would be ideal.

Appreciate it — our deadline for the questionnaire is Friday.

Regards,
Sarah
Sarah Cole
Information Security - BrightBank
[Attachment: BBQ_vendor_qs_v3.pdf (pdf)]

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Cole <sarah.cole@brightbank.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-03-20T14:45:00-04:00
Subject: Re: Quick clarification on what Redwood keeps by default (requests vs outputs)

Hi Sarah — thanks for the clear asks. Below is a concise, customer-friendly summary you can include in BrightBank's memo. I'm copying Jonas (AE) for commercial context and Priyom (engineering lead) for precise technical notes and the matrix attachment.

Quick summary (plain language):
- Prompts/request text: By default we retain request text for 30 days to support troubleshooting, abuse investigations, and quality monitoring. Requests older than 30 days are deleted unless a customer elects longer retention or is on a Reserved/Dedicated plan.
- Generated outputs/completions: Default retention is 90 days for generated outputs to enable quality review and model improvements; customers can opt out or mark outputs as ephemeral.
- Streaming fragments and KV cache: Streaming fragments (intermediate token buffers) and ephemeral KV cache are treated as transient and removed within 24 hours by default; they are not permanently indexed.
- Attachments & uploaded files: Any files uploaded as part of a request follow the same retention flags as the request; we surface them in the console for the retention window and then purge.

Three-line capture matrix (copy/paste friendly):
- Request text (prompts): retained 30d by default (metadata kept longer for billing/metrics), can opt out.
- Model outputs (finalized completions): retained 90d by default, opt-out/ephemeral flag available.
- Streaming fragments/KV cache: ephemeral, purged <=24h by default; not considered part of long-term logs.

A few important notes:
- Customers can request immediate deletion for their account via the Console or by contacting support; we provide proof-of-deletion logs for compliance requests.
- For Dedicated/Private deployments we support custom retention and on-premise storage options to meet regulatory requirements.
- EU data residency: if BrightBank requires EU-only residency, records are stored in EU regions and retention windows are applied within that region.

I'll attach a short technical matrix next. If you want slightly different window numbers for procurement language (e.g., 45d instead of 30d for prompts), tell me and we'll align with legal.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Director, Compliance — Redwood Inference

Sarah — adding a commercial note so your procurement team sees the options up-front:

- Hosted (default) customers: the windows Kimberly listed are standard (30d prompts / 90d outputs).
- Reserved / Dedicated: we can commit to custom windows as part of the contract (e.g., 0d prompt retention or 30d outputs) and include SLA language.
- Private/VPC/on-prem: customer-managed; Redwood provides the tooling to purge and evidence deletion on request.

I'll also cc our support channel on the formal questionnaire response. Attaching the short FAQ we share with procurement — it includes the delete request playbook.

From: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.ai>

Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Quick clarification on what Redwood keeps by default (requests vs outputs)

Sarah / team — adding the precise, engineer-oriented detail you can drop into your security assessment if you want exact behavior.

Default behavior (hosted API):
- Ingress records: we persist request headers + metadata indefinitely for billing/metrics (customer_id, model_id, token counts). The raw prompt text is stored in a short-lived store (30d) unless a customer toggles the "no-store"/ephemeral flag.
- Final outputs: stored in long-term object storage (90d) with lifecycle rules that transition older objects to immediate deletion. Outputs marked with an Ephemeral flag are written to ephemeral storage and removed at session end.
- Streaming/KV: streaming token buffers are kept in in-memory caches and written to short-term buffer storage only when necessary for fault-tolerance; by configuration these buffers expire in <=24h and are not indexed for search.
- Deletion workflow: a delete request triggers (1) immediate tombstone of the logical record, (2) background expunge that removes object storage blobs within 24–72 hours, (3) issuance of a signed proof-of-deletion report (hashes + timestamps) available in the Console or via our support portal.
- Proofs & audit: we maintain immutable audit logs for deletion actions (who requested, API key used, timestamps) for 1 year to satisfy audit needs; the audit log contains pointers but not raw prompt text after deletion.

Examples you can paste: 
- "A hosted request with default settings: BrightBank prompt stored 30 days; model output stored 90 days; both can be erased on request; proof-of-deletion available in Console."
- "If you enable Ephemeral mode at the request level: prompt and output not written to durable object storage; session buffers cleared at session end (~seconds to minutes)."

Related links for your team:
- Retention matrix (spreadsheet): https://drive.google.com/drive/fake-retention-matrix
- Support request template / evidence flow: HBSP-45678

If you want, we can convert this into a single-page statement of default capture behavior for your vendor risk spreadsheet.
